newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks fade to finish little changed.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks fade to finish little changed.

text.p: SPI futures 2759 -3 US 30yr cl 6.49 -0.01
10yrbond futs 93.520 +0.035 Gold NY 326.00 Lon fix 326.55
*Stocks end with narrow gains, late selling pares early modest rate cut-inspired gains. Volume 344.35 million, A$818.16 value, 1,135 stocks traded, 321 steady, 439 up, 375 down.
Australian shares faded to finish little changed on Wednesday after a cut in interest rates proved to be an anti-climax with the market widely anticipating the Reserve Bank's actions.
The All Ordinaries index edged up 3.1 points to 2,735, while September share price index futures contracts lost three points to 2,759, a 24 point premium to the underlying ndex.

The Reserve Bank of Australia reduced the official cash rate by 0.5 of a percentage point to 5.0 percent, citing good inflation and wages data. The cut lifted the market early before sellers moved in to trim the moderate gains in choppy trade.
The selling that emerged failed to surprise traders with so many having already factored a rate reduction into their buying after key wages and inflation data last week.
"Everyone had been getting excited about it over the last few days," said dealer Grant Williams of Reynolds and Co, a stance also adopted by others.
"The decision to do it today may have surprised but most figured it was due in a matter of days anyway," said a Brisbane-based broker.
ANZ Bank and Westpac Banking Corp starred early, hitting new highs before fading as sellers stepped in.
ANZ peaked at A$10.76 before easing to close 11 cents higher at A$10.70, while Westpac surged to A$8.65 before retreating to close just 4.1 cents higher at A$8.511.
National Australia Bank was steady for much of the day before profit-takers cashed in with a bout of afternoon selling that sliced 17 cents off the sector leader to see it close at A$19.61.
Commonwealth Bank jumped 22 cents early but also attracted sellers near the top and ended just one cent higher at A$16.69.

In the miners, zinc producer Pasminco slid three percent lower to close at A$2.60 with brokers blaming the slump in the nickel price in London trade, although they noted the volatile metals prices generally.
"It was a big drop (in zinc) but the metals prices have been volatile," Reynold's Williams said.

Golds shone early before coming back to the pack, the index climbing 1.3 percent early before easing to close up half a percent. Brokers said some bargain hunting amid talk of a bid by Canadian giant Barrick Gold Corp for Joe Gutnick's Great Central had underpinned the sector interest.
"The Great Central talk might be highlighting how cheap some of our major gold stocks are," said a Brisbane-based dealer.
Best performed included Great Central, up 10 cents to A$2.80, Resolute Ltd added 4.9 percent to A$1.93, while a thinly traded Goldfields added 5.6 percent to A$1.70.

Elsewhere, Alan Jackson's investment and manufacturing Austrim Ltd remained keenly sought, adding another 22 cents to A$4.79. The company has now leapt over 24 percent since Monday's announcement of a surge in full year net profit to A$21.91 million and a 2-for-5 rights issue.

"It has been very hard to get set in some of these second line industrials like Austrim which has seen some good volume go through. That is one stock where it hasn't mattered what the market has done," Reynold's Williams said.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about six to five, while about 28 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
Futures trade was active with 8,263 September SPI contracts traded. Options trade was modest with 31,884 options traded.
The Australian 10-year bond yield finished only modestly lower as profit-taking reversed the immediate plunge which followed the 1/2 point rate cut by the Reserve Bank.
By 5.25 p.m. (0725 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 6.52 percent, compared to Tuesday's 6.54 percent.

The Australian dollar breezed through the rate cut to finish a cent higher as bulls finally scented an end to policy uncertainty. By 5.25 p.m. (0725 GMT), the dollar had romped to US$0.7470/75, its best local close in three weeks, having briefly dipped 1/2 cent to US$0.7395 immediately after the RBA announcement hit dealing screens.
